title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
description:
Core skills: Product Marketing, GTM Strategy, Growth, Analyst Relations, Thought Leadership, Narrative Design, AI-Driven Marketing

At Bitmovin , we empower developers to build the future of video. As a global leader in video infrastructure, our solutions power streaming platforms like Netflix, BBC, and Hulu. We are seeking a Senior Product Marketing & Growth Lead who is a strategist and a storyteller at heart. You won’t just manage frameworks—you will shape our market identity, drive our growth engine, and define how the world understands the value of our video infrastructure.

“We are constantly seeking out forward thinking individuals who want to shape the future of video… come and work with us!” Stefan Lederer, CEO

At Bitmovin we value cognitive diversity and the huge part this plays in not only creating a global culture second to none, but in how this underpins our ability to create truly representative, Emmy award winning products. Diversity in all its forms is encouraged and celebrated at Bitmovin; everyone has a role to play in helping us shape the future of video.

The Role

This is a high-impact leadership role where "doing" is just as important as "directing." As our Senior Product Marketing & Growth Lead, you will operate at two levels: defining the long-term strategic vision and getting your h ands dirty in the execution. You are the vital bridge between Product, Marketing, and Sales, ensuring that our technical innovations translate into market-leading narratives and high-performing campaigns.

Reporting to the CPO and working in lockstep with the VP of Marketing, you will own the "truth" of how Bitmovin shows up in the market, transforming complex technical capabilities into compelling growth stories.

What You Will Build:

-
Define & Own Strategic Positioning: Lead market sizing, segmentation, and competitive positioning across all product lines. You will ensure Bitmovin isn't just a technical choice, but the definitive category leader in video infrastructure.

-
Architect GTM & Campaigns: Own the full go-to-market strategy for product launches. You will develop the briefs, messaging frameworks, and success metrics that empower the broader Marketing team to execute world-class campaigns.

-
Drive Analyst Relations: Build and own relationships with key industry firms. You will shape our positioning in analyst reports and ensure Bitmovin remains the "innovation leader" in the eyes of the market’s most influential voices.

-
Be a Visible External Voice: Act as a primary spokesperson for Bitmovin. Whether it’s presenting on stage at major conferences, leading media briefings, or participating in industry panels, you will be the face and voice of our market evolution.

-
Scale with AI: Actively integrate AI tools into your workflow to move faster—from competitive intelligence and research to rapid content iteration and campaign optimization.

-
Enable the Revenue Engine: Partner with Sales and Product leads to create the narrative tools that close deals. You’ll ensure our technical value is translated into clear, differentiated outcomes for buyers and decision-makers.

What can you bring

-
Proven Leadership: 8+ years in Product Marketing or Growth roles, with at least 2 years in a senior leadership or lead capacity within the B2B tech space.

-
Technical Fluency: A background in OTT streaming media technology (Live, VOD, AdTech. You don’t need to be a developer, but you must be able to earn the respect of engineers and translate "bits and bytes" into "business value."

-
A "Builder" Mindset: A track record of doing the work, not just managing it. You are a world-class writer, a sharp messenger, and a hands-on executor of GTM strategies.

-
AI Curiosity: You are already using AI tools in your daily work and are excited about pushing the boundaries of how these technologies can accelerate marketing and growth.

-
Public Presence: You are comfortable—and thrive—as a public-facing spokesperson, with the ability to distill complex concepts into narratives that resonate with analysts and executives alike.

-
Collaborative Spirit: You build bridges across Product, Revenue, and Engineering, understanding that great positioning only lands when it is cross-functionally aligned.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the Role

As a Senior DevOps Engineer at Ledgy, you'll build the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably. You'll join our Platform team, collaborating with engineers and InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure for a product that helps companies manage equity.

Our challenge is to make delivery faster, production easier to operate, and AI-assisted development safer - while keeping complexity and costs in check.

Location: We hire remotely across Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania.

The team you'll join: Platform - Builds the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably, working with InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure.

What You'll Work On

- Cloud infrastructure. Evolve our GCP and Kubernetes cloud architecture and setup with Terraform, improving reliability, simplicity, and cost visibility and enabling scaling to multiple availability regions.

- CI/CD and developer experience. Speed up feedback loops, reduce flaky builds, and turn recurring support requests into self-service tooling.

- Observability. Reduce alert noise, define meaningful SLOs, and make production issues easier to diagnose.

- Security and automation. Partner with InfoSec on secure delivery, access controls, and guardrails for AI-assisted workflows.

You'll also join our incident-response on-call rotation during working hours and help prevent recurring issues. As we expand our servicing of public companies and jurisdictions, this on-call might evolve to compensated 24h/7 hour rotation.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. These are the things that would make you an especially good fit.

- Have strong DevOps / SRE background designing and operating cloud infrastructure and production systems

- Have worked with Kubernetes and infrastructure as code, ideally GCP and Terraform

- Enjoy building fast, reliable CI/CD pipelines and improving developer experience

- Can diagnose issues across networking, infrastructure, and application code

- Write maintainable code and bring a practical approach to observability and security

- Value collaboration, mentorship, and thoughtful trade-offs between reliability, complexity, and cost

- Are curious about supporting AI-assisted development safely - no AI specialism required

Experience with Node.js, MongoDB or Temporal is a plus.

Our Tech Stack

We work in TypeScript: React, Tailwind CSS, and tRPC on the front end, and tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, and Temporal on the back end. Infrastructure runs on GCP, Terraform Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, and GitHub Actions. For observability and incident response we use Grafana, Sentry, and PagerDuty.

You don't need to know all of it. We don't expect proficiency in every part of this stack. Strong infrastructure fundamentals and the ability to learn matter more than knowing every tool already.

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First 30 days:

- Get to know Ledgy, the Platform team, and our internal users with an onboarding buddy

- Explore our infrastructure and delivery workflows, and ship your first improvement

- Analyze current state of our cloud infrastructure and propose meaningful enhancements

First 3 months:

- Independently deliver improvements to CI/CD, observability, or infrastructure design

- Share operational ownership and help reduce recurring friction for engineers

- Contribute to architecture discussions and document what others need to operate our systems

First 6-12 months:

- Own DevOps and SRE function and DevOps initiatives from problem definition through rollout and adoption

- Deliver measurable improvements to developer experience, reliability, or cost

- Help shape our platform's direction and mentor other engineers

The interview process

- Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role

- Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.

- System Design (60 min): A system design session where you will design an architecture for a problem from the Ledgy domain using a visual tool of your choice

- DDSA (45 min): A Deep Dive into real System Architecture that you have built, owned and monitored.

- Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy's mission and values

 - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register.



We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

🎯 Your main goal will be to identify and reduce security risks across n8n's product and internal systems, using threat modelling, hands-on security expertise, and cross-functional collaboration to help teams design, build, and operate more secure systems.

You'll join our growing security team at a pivotal stage, acting as a trusted security partner to teams across the business. You'll help us build a move from reactive security management to a proactive, scalable security practice.

Here's what you'll be driving:


THREAT MODELLING, RISK ASSESSMENT & SECURITY DESIGN

 - Conduct threat modelling and risk assessments across product features, AI agents, cloud infrastructure, corporate IT, internal applications, and data systems, identifying vulnerabilities and recommending practical mitigations.

 - Partner with Engineering, Cloud, IT, and Data teams to review security designs, define actionable security requirements, and influence the implementation of appropriate controls.

 - Help teams embed security into their development processes through secure coding guidance, design reviews, documentation, and security tooling that enables them to identify and address risks independently.


VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT & COORDINATED DISCLOSURE

 - Participate in the security triage rotation, assessing incoming vulnerability reports, validating findings, and prioritising remediation based on severity and business impact.

 - Collaborate with engineering teams to coordinate vulnerability remediation, verify fixes, and support secure patch and release processes.

 - Help manage our vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty programmes, including engagement with security researchers, coordinated disclosures, and GitHub Security Advisories.


SECURITY OPERATIONS & INCIDENT READINESS

 - Help establish and improve logging, detection, and protective monitoring capabilities across our infrastructure, corporate systems, and internal applications.

 - Develop and improve incident response processes, runbooks, and exercises to strengthen our ability to detect, investigate, and respond to security incidents.

 - Work closely with system owners to identify security gaps, prioritise remediation, and verify that implemented controls effectively reduce risk.


CUSTOMER TRUST & COMPLIANCE ENGINEERING

 - Support SOC 2 compliance by helping establish continuous control monitoring, automated evidence collection, and processes that make security assurance part of everyday operations.

 - Collaborate with Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success to respond to customer security assessments and build reusable resources that streamline future requests.

 - Partner with Legal, Finance, IT, and other stakeholders to assess security risks, improve security policies and controls, and strengthen trust with enterprise customers.

We're hiring two Security Engineers with complementary strengths, so you don't need to be an expert in every security domain. 


REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

 - 🔍 Threat Modelling & Risk Assessment: You have hands-on experience assessing real-world systems, identifying security risks, determining defensible severity levels, and recommending practical controls that teams can implement.

n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems you tackle as a designer are complex. Your design decisions must account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes impact the entire platform. To thrive here, you will need to love talking to users, understanding technology, and reducing complexity and scope.

You'll be embedded in a product squad alongside a product manager, engineering manager and around three to five engineers, owning the user experience for your area end to end. Our design team is small but growing, so you'll shape the craft bar and the culture, not inherit them.

We're hiring designers across the following teams:

 - Enterprise (two roles: Governance & Observability, and Licence & Billing): You've worked on technical B2B platforms. You've designed for scale, governance and collaboration across teams, including permissions, environments, observability and failure modes, and you're comfortable making deeply complex systems feel coherent and simple. Governance & Observability gives admins visibility and the controls to enforce how n8n is used, from audit logging and execution diagnostics to admin settings. Licence & Billing covers licensing, subscriptions, usage-based billing and the cloud admin experience.

 - Knowledge: You have exceptional product sense and can connect disparate elements into a coherent whole. You'll take something complex, with many moving parts, and make it make sense. The team works on how agents and automations access company knowledge, and on core workflow-building surfaces such as data tables, sub-workflow execution and the canvas. Experience with data visualisation is welcome; deep technical expertise isn't required.

 - n8n Labs: As a Product Designer, you'll own discovery end to end: spotting the riskiest assumptions, running the research and turning findings into decisions without waiting on a brief. You move fast, cut scope without losing what matters, and you're hands-on enough to build and ship your own prototypes, including using AI tools to get there quicker. You've got product and business judgement, not just craft; you can spot an opportunity and make the case for it. Founder or co-founder experience is a helpful signal but not a requirement.

Team assignment is confirmed at the offer stage and may be subject to change as the team structure evolves.



🎯 Regardless of the team, your main goal will be to lead end-to-end product design on complex workflows that elevate n8n's user experience, ship measurable outcomes, and raise the quality bar across our platform. To do so, here are your responsibilities:

End-to-end product design

 - Lead the full design process for your team, from discovery to polished delivery, collaborating closely with PMs and engineers.

 - Consistently ship high-quality, visually cohesive designs that improve the overall UX at every release.

 - Work effectively on complex features and understand the underlying technology.

 - Take ownership of complex, multi-faceted problems and drive them to completion with initiative and autonomy.

Research, feedback, and UX quality

 - Own the direction of research for your team: decide when it's needed, choose the right methodology, and take the initiative without waiting to be told.

 - Champion the user by talking to them regularly and running research that informs critical product and business decisions.

 - Master the feedback loop by gathering, synthesising and acting on input while giving actionable critique to elevate teammates' work.

 - Balance speed and quality in an MVP-driven environment, navigating ambiguity while maintaining a high bar.

Systems thinking and platform coherence

 - Design in systems, integrating solutions into the broader n8n platform and safeguarding the product's big picture.

 - Account for edge cases, constraints and interaction details so users never end up in impossible states.

 - Collaborate across teams and designers to ensure consistency and quality across shared patterns and components.

Strategy, impact, and innovation

 - Shape team strategy by influencing planning, prioritisation and scope with a strong design perspective tied to KPIs.

 - Explore and adopt AI and automation tools to push the boundaries of design practice and AI-powered workflows.

Senior or Staff?

We're open at multiple levels and we'll calibrate with you during the process, based on the scope you've operated at. At Senior, you own your squad's design end to end and ship work that raises the bar for your area. At Staff, you do that, and your influence reaches beyond your own squad: you shape patterns other designers build on, and you take on the problems that span teams. All levels are hands-on: this is not a step away from the craft.

 - 🏗️ Complex product experience: You've designed complex, information-dense products, ideally technical B2B web products. Consumer-only or mobile-only portfolios are unlikely to be the right fit.

 - 🧠 Technical mindset: You collaborate effectively with engineers and understand how software is built, including common web technologies. You don't need to write code, but you do need genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath: APIs, webhooks, data structures and how workflows actually execute.

 - 🧭 Ownership & delivery: You've shipped end-to-end features in smaller teams or startups and can drive complex problems to measurable outcomes.

 - ⚡ Fast, focused execution: You operate at high speed in an MVP-driven environment, balancing quality and velocity amid ambiguity.

 - 📈 Outcome orientation: You use research and metrics to inform decisions and consistently deliver solutions that enable team KPIs.

 - 🤝 Feedback & collaboration: You're open and non-defensive in critique and provide actionable feedback that raises the team's bar.

 - 🧪 Curiosity for AI: You're enthusiastic about AI and innovation, actively exploring new tools and approaches to advance the craft.

 - 📅 Experience level: You have 5+ years in product design with demonstrable impact on shipped products.



Nice-to-haves

OWN THE QUALITY BAR

 - Evolve the design system and QA practices so the bar rises as the team grows.

 - Dig into one of the most genuinely interesting UX challenges in the space: n8n has historically had a steep learning curve for new users. Your job is to lower that floor without losing the power that experienced builders love.


DRIVE DESIGN'S STRATEGIC INFLUENCE

 - Shape product strategy, not just respond to it. Bring design thinking into roadmap conversations and help surface user problems before they become someone else's brief.

 - Help lead n8n's expansion toward a broader, less technical audience, a deliberate and exciting strategic shift that design should be leading.

 - Build the kind of relationships with Product, Engineering, and leadership where design is a genuine thought partner at every stage.


BUILD AND GROW THE TEAM

 - Lead a team of around 14 designers today: 2 Design Leads each working with ~6 ICs, plus Design Engineering and UX Research (with more hires ahead).

 - Shape the team structure, career framework, and progression paths so people know where they stand and where they're going.

 - Create a culture of high standards and honest feedback, where people feel supported to do their best work and have a clear sense of what great looks like.

 - Own hiring and headcount planning for the department, and help us grow without losing what makes the team good.


BUILD RESEARCH INTO HOW WE MAKE DECISIONS

 - Establish a pragmatic, continuous research practice from the ground up. We're making our first dedicated UX research hires, so there's real room to shape this.

 - Make customer insight, product data, and community feedback a live input to product decisions, so teams are building from evidence at every step.

 - Connect research to the decisions that matter most: activation, adoption, retention, and helping new users find their way into n8n with confidence.

 - Champion practical AI adoption inside the design org, from prototyping and research synthesis to design QA and workflow efficiency.

 - Help the team stay curious and current as the tools, patterns, and expectations around AI products continue to evolve fast.

 - Model the kind of working style you want to see: thoughtful, adaptive, and genuinely excited about what's changing.

 - 🎨 Craft authority: You are a quality bar, not just someone who appreciates quality. You can identify great work, explain why it's great, and hold the line on standards even when it's uncomfortable.

 - 📣 Strategic influence, not just strategic thinking: You have made design a co-equal in product conversations, not a downstream function. You know how to bring people with you, create debate, and drive decisions.

 - 🔀 Structured problem-solving under ambiguity: You find your way into unclear problems and create a plan. You don't just ask good questions, you answer them. You move forward when there's no map.

 - 🤖 AI-era product judgment: You understand the AI, automation, or adjacent tooling landscape and can turn emerging patterns into usable, trustworthy product experiences.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.



Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:



 - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

 - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

 - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register.



We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Your mission: drive ARR growth by turning hundreds (soon thousands) of n8n agency partners into a demand engine through scaled marketing programs.

Our agency partner network includes automation specialists and small consultancies with most ranging from 1–50 people. They leverage n8n to help their customers automate and transform their business - they have technical skills and customer knowledge but most have limited marketing resources.

The goal for this position is to define, build and launch creative marketing programs that our agency partners can utilize to grow their business with n8n. This will include building scalable self-serve programs (one to many) as well as working with some of the larger agency partners on specific marketing programs (one to one). Here’s an overview of what this position will be responsible for: 

Build the program portfolio - Drive adoption

 - Work directly with the agency partner marketing managers to define the overall strategy - what playbooks, what investments, what markets etc.

 - Ship ready-to-run programs: Event-in-a-Box kits for local workshops and seminars, email and social campaigns, industry-specific use-case campaigns, reusable customer stories and simple demand-gen playbooks.

 - Make every program executable without help: clear steps, editable templates and localisable assets that work for a solo consultant and a 50-person agency, in any region.

 - Drive awareness and adoption of the various marketing programs through scaled and creative communications.

Measure and multiply

 - Track the full funnel from access to download, execution, customer opportunities and revenue — for partners and for n8n.

 - Use partner feedback and performance data to decide what to scale, what to change and what to stop.

 - Turn each working program into a repeatable model for the next one, and automate your own program operations with n8n where it saves time.

 - Measure the overall business impact and growth from agency partner generated business.
   
   

Requirements 

Must-have

 - Partner marketing at scale: You've built one-to-many programs adopted by hundreds or thousands of partners, and can show adoption numbers

 - Self-service program design: You've packaged marketing so non-marketers can run it (kits, templates, playbooks) and know what makes them get used rather than downloaded

 - Small-business empathy: You understand how small consultancies work and design for their limited time, budget and marketing know-how

 - Outcome-driven measurement: You measure execution and pipeline, not asset views, and you're comfortable stopping a program that isn't working

 - Bias for action: You're happy as a first hire with limited design and development support; you ship a pilot quickly and improve it with real data

 - Global mindset: You've run programs across several regions and segments, and know how to localise without rebuilding from scratch

 

Nice-to-have

 - Strategic partner programs: You've also built custom marketing programs with large partners that ran over several months or quarters

 - Channel or ecosystem background: You've worked on an agency, solutions-partner or reseller program at a software company

 - Hands-on with automation: You've built workflows yourself — in n8n or similar tools — and can talk shop with technical partners

 - Local events: You've designed field events or workshops that others delivered

 - Languages: You work professionally in a language beyond English

n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n https://www.notion.so/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35?pvs=21 (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Please apply to the location you're the most likely to work from in the future. 




BENEFITS 

 - Competitive compensation 💸 – We offer fair and attractive pay.

 - Ownership 💪 – Our core value is to “empower others,” and we mean it—you’ll get a slice of n8n with equity.

 - Work/life balance 🏖️ – We work hard but ensure you have time to recharge:
   
   - Europe: 30 days of vacation, plus public holidays wherever you are.
   
   - US: 20 vacation days, 8 sick days, plus public holidays wherever you are.

 - Health & wellness 🩺 –
   
   - Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*
   
   - US: Multiple low-premium, low-deductible medical plans with coverage for individuals and families—plus a no-cost premium HDHP option with a pre-seeded HSA—along with dental and vision coverage.

 - Future planning 💰 –
   
   - Europe: We provide pension contributions according to local country norms.*
   
   - US: 401(k) retirement plan with a 4% employer match.

 - Financial security 🛡️ –
   
   - Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*
   
   - US: Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance, plus life insurance to support you and your loved ones.

 - Career growth 📈 – We hire rising stars who grow with us! You’ll get €1K (or equivalent) per year to spend on courses, books, events, or coaching to level up your skills.

 - A passionate team 🤩 – We love our product, and we prove it with regular hackathons where we see who can build the coolest thing with it!

 - Remote-first 🌏 – Our team works remotely across Europe, with regular off-sites for team bonding. Some roles, like sales in the US, are hybrid—please check the job description.

 - Giving back 🤝 – We're big fans of open source, and you'll get $100 per month to support projects you care about.

 - Transparency 🙏 – We all know what everyone’s working on, how the company is doing—the whole shebang.

 - Excellent product & UX judgment: You’re known for simplifying complexity and have a strong instinct for what makes technical products intuitive, polished, and enjoyable to use.

 - Technical fluency: You’re comfortable reasoning about APIs, integrations, authentication, schemas, data flows, and system constraints and can partner deeply with engineers.

 - Strong product discovery skills: You get close to users, uncover the underlying problem behind feature requests, validate assumptions, and turn insights into focused product decisions.

 - Data fluency: You can define meaningful success metrics, investigate product behaviour and funnels, and combine quantitative evidence with qualitative insight and product intuition 

 - AI-native product thinking: You actively use modern AI tools in your own work and understand the opportunities and product challenges created by AI-powered experiences.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Developer product experience: You’ve built products for technical users and understand what great developer and builder experiences look like.

 - Integrations experience: You’ve worked on products involving third-party APIs, authentication, developer platforms, or integration ecosystems.

 - Community or open-source experience: You’ve built products alongside developer communities, contributors, or external ecosystems.

 - AI product experience: You’ve worked with LLMs, agents, model providers, evaluations, or other AI platform capabilities and understand their unique product tradeoffs.

 - Experimentation experience: You know how to use prototypes, experiments, and incremental releases to learn quickly without adding unnecessary process.

 - Cloud/SaaS experience: You understand the reliability, scalability, security, and enterprise considerations involved in building critical SaaS products.



Why join us?

At n8n, you’ll work on the heart of the product experience - shaping how builders go from an idea to a workflow they trust in production. Your work will influence some of the most fundamental parts of n8n: how people build, connect services, access powerful capabilities, understand what’s happening in their workflows, and scale from simple automation to complex AI-powered systems.



You’ll join n8n at a stage where the product and company are scaling rapidly, but there is still enormous opportunity to define what a world-class automation building experience should feel like. You’ll have the autonomy to identify important problems, work deeply with users and technical teams, and turn ambitious ideas into product experiences people rely on every day.

🎯 Your main goal will be to own the forward-looking financial plan for the top and mid funnel of n8n’s commercial engine, helping Marketing leadership make sharper investment decisions across both our PLG and SLG motions.

To do so, you’ll turn demand, funnel, and marketing investment decisions into an integrated financial view that leadership can act on:


OWN MARKETING PLANNING & FORECASTING

 - Drive n8n’s annual planning and regular forecasting process for Marketing end to end, from top-down targets and cross-functional alignment through regional segmentation, budget ownership, and consolidation into the company plan.

 - Partner with Marketing budget owners across demand generation, brand, community and DevRel, product marketing, and events to set budgets, forecast spend, and sharpen investment trade-offs.

 - Own program spend with the same rigor as headcount, including agency and media contracts, event and sponsorship commitments, phasing, seasonality, and in-year reallocations.


MODEL FUNNEL & CHANNEL ECONOMICS

 - Model demand creation, signup and MQL volume, activation, qualified opportunity, conversion, and velocity with Marketing Ops and RevOps across both PLG and SLG motions.

 - Translate funnel and channel levers into the demand assumptions behind n8n’s integrated top-line model and quantify the financial impact and trade-offs of changing them.

 - Assess CAC and payback, conversion, pipeline contribution, and expected versus realized ROI using attribution, incrementality testing, and other causal methods where appropriate.


BUILD A RIGOROUS MARKETING INVESTMENT FRAMEWORK

 - Establish a repeatable process for material marketing bets covering hypothesis, baseline, expected return, confidence range, leading indicators, scale-or-stop triggers, and post-investment review.

 - Build and defend investment cases for brand, community, content, events, and other spend that does not attribute cleanly to closed revenue.

 - Use internal evidence, external benchmarks, and post-investment learnings to drive in-year reallocations toward the highest-impact opportunities.


TURN DATA INTO DECISIONS

 - Partner with Marketing Ops, RevOps, Data, and Controlling to keep the financial view aligned with n8n’s attribution, measurement, and reporting frameworks.

 - Own the financial metric definitions behind Marketing reporting and ensure teams are operating from a consistent view of performance.

 - Turn financial reporting and variance analysis into tangible insights and recommendations for Marketing leadership, executives, and board-level audiences when needed.


REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

 - 📊 FP&A experience: You have 7+ years of experience in FP&A or strategic finance, ideally in a fast-paced technology or B2B SaaS environment.

 - 🗂️ Complex planning experience: You have led complex, multi-entity, multi-stakeholder annual planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes end to end.

 - 🤝 Marketing business partnering: You have deep demand-side finance partnering experience in either a self-serve/PLG funnel or an enterprise/SLG demand generation motion, plus a strong working understanding of the other.

 - 📈 Funnel and channel economics: You are fluent in CAC and CAC payback by channel and motion, blended versus paid CAC, CLV/CAC, pipeline attribution, funnel conversion, and velocity.

 - 🧭 Judgment on unattributable spend: You have built and defended investment cases for brand, community, content, or similar spend that will never attribute cleanly to a closed deal.

 - 💶 Program spend ownership: You are comfortable owning a budget weighted toward program spend, including commitments, phasing, agency costs, vendor economics, and reallocations.

 - 🧮 Financial modeling: You build sophisticated, integrated financial models that remain robust as assumptions, scenarios, and operating inputs change.

 - 🗣️ Executive communication: You translate complex analysis into clear recommendations and are comfortable presenting to Marketing leadership, executives, and board audiences when needed.

 - 🤖 AI- and automation-first mindset: You naturally use AI and automation platforms such as n8n to improve the quality, speed, and repeatability of your planning, reporting, and analysis.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - 🔄 PLG + SLG fluency: You have deep experience across both product-led and sales-led demand motions rather than primarily one.

 - 🧑‍💻 Developer-focused environment: You have worked at a community-led, open-source, or developer-focused product company.

 - 🧪 Incrementality & experimentation: You have exposure to incrementality testing, holdout design, or marketing mix modeling.

 - 🛠️ Marketing & RevOps tooling: You have experience consuming data from tools such as HubSpot or Marketo, GA4, attribution platforms, and Salesforce.

 - 📋 Planning platforms: You have worked with financial or headcount planning platforms such as Pigment in complex, multi-entity, or multi-stakeholder environments.

 - 🧑‍🔬 Data self-sufficiency: You are comfortable using SQL and building your own views in tools such as Looker, Metabase, or Hex rather than waiting on a Data team.

 - ⚙️ Relevant SaaS domain experience: You have worked in workflow automation, developer tools, or infrastructure SaaS.

Why join us?

At n8n, you’ll own the financial view of one of the most important joins in our growth engine: where community, product-led adoption, and enterprise demand generation meet. You’ll work closely with Marketing leadership and counterpart FP&A Managers covering the PLG and SLG bottom of funnel, giving you visibility across the full commercial plan and real influence over how we allocate one of our largest discretionary investments.

You’ll join a fast-growing, remote-first company where finance is expected to help shape decisions, not simply report on them. As n8n expands the opportunity around AI agent orchestration and helps businesses unlock measurable ROI through automation, you’ll help build the planning discipline, investment frameworks, and automation-first finance practices that support our next stage of growth.

Sound like a challenge you’re excited to take on?

Apply now — and help us build the future of automation.

To do so, you’ll work directly with customers, Deployment Strategists, and Product to make every engagement high-impact, scalable, and repeatable:


Drive high-impact enterprise deployments

Embed on-site with enterprise customers for focused 5-day deployment engagements, arriving with a hypothesis and leaving with production workflows in place.

Partner closely with Deployment Strategists to align technical execution with customer priorities, stakeholder needs, and adoption goals.

Build trust with technical and non-technical stakeholders by turning complex customer environments into clear, actionable solutions.


Build production-grade automation solutions

Design and build workflows, integrations, and custom nodes tailored to each customer’s environment and scalable beyond the initial use case.

Extend existing n8n nodes or add missing functionality where needed to unlock high-value enterprise use cases.

Translate ambiguous business problems into concrete automation designs that prioritize real customer value over technical complexity.

Work across industries and tech stacks, getting productive quickly in new environments.


Bridge customer needs with Product and Engineering

Identify when a bespoke customer requirement should become a reusable node improvement, product feature, or platform capability.

Create a clear feedback loop with Product and Engineering by documenting technical gaps, customer context, implementation learnings, and prioritization signals.

Contribute reusable learnings, workflows, custom nodes, and integration patterns to an internal playbook library.


Turn customer learnings into product and playbooks

Identify when a bespoke customer requirement should become a core product feature and document it clearly for Product.

Contribute reusable learnings, workflows, and patterns to an internal playbook library.

Help ensure every engagement makes the next one faster, stronger, and more productized.


Keep engagements focused and scalable

Deliver time-boxed customer engagements with clear outcomes, rather than open-ended professional services work.

Build solutions that customers can own and operate themselves.

Know when to build, when to simplify, and when to push back to avoid unnecessary complexity.

Must-haves

🧑‍💻 Strong engineering background: You have solid full-stack or backend engineering experience and have built integrations, APIs, or automation pipelines in production environments.

🧩 Integration-building expertise: You can create custom nodes, extend existing integrations, and work confidently with APIs, authentication patterns, data models, and event-driven systems.

🔧 Product-minded technical execution: You can distinguish between a one-off customer workaround, a reusable node improvement, and a product feature worth escalating.

🤝 Customer-facing confidence: You’re comfortable working directly in customer environments and can build trust with engineers, operators, and non-technical stakeholders.

🗺️ Solution design skills: You can take a messy operational problem and turn it into a clean, practical technical design.

⚖️ Strong technical judgment: You know when to build, when to push back, and how to avoid gold-plating solutions that should stay simple.

✈️ Willingness to travel: You’re open to travelling roughly 30-50% of the time for on-site engagements, primarily across Europe.

⚡ Speed to productive: You can quickly understand new industries, tech stacks, and customer environments without needing everything to be neatly defined.



Nice-to-haves

🔁 Workflow automation experience: You have familiarity with n8n or similar workflow automation tools.

🏢 Enterprise deployment experience: You’ve worked with strategic enterprise accounts in complex technical environments.

Today these live across several teams and two billing stacks; you'll bring them into one stable home that the rest of the company builds on.



This is a foundations role. You build the system that pricing and packaging decisions run on, rather than running price experiments yourself. To do so, here are your core responsibilities:



OWN THE LICENSING & BILLING STRATEGY & ROADMAP

 - Define and communicate the product strategy and roadmap for Licensing & Billing in partnership with Engineering, Product leadership, Finance, and go-to-market.

 - Prioritize foundational investments based on revenue integrity, enterprise needs, data correctness, and engineering effort, and make trade-offs explicit.

 - Lead discovery with enterprise customers, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and RevOps to understand how n8n is bought, renewed, and grown today, and where that breaks.



LICENSING, ENTITLEMENTS & ACCOUNTS

 - Own the license server and entitlement model: issuance, renewal, and validation across Cloud, self-hosted, air-gapped, and OEM deployments, with one source of truth for which plan or deal grants which features.

 - Introduce "account" as a first-class product primitive (accounts, purchases, license keys, activations) and expose it as the API contract our customer-facing console and multi-instance management are built on.

 - Productize the deal-to-entitlement flow so a closed deal in Salesforce creates or updates entitlements without manual steps.



METERING & BILLING PLATFORM

 - Own usage metering and billing for Cloud and Enterprise, including subscription billing: what counts as a billable execution, quota consumption, and overage charging.

 - Lead the migration off Paddle Classic and unify Cloud and Enterprise billing into one platform.

 - Build the mechanics for usage-based enterprise billing and reliable overage charging.



CROSS-ORG ALIGNMENT

 - Make the architecture and mechanism decisions (entitlement model, billing platform, enterprise invoicing path) and align closely with Finance and go-to-market on each of them. Every decision here touches money; you bring people along rather than inform them afterwards.

 - Hold clear boundaries with adjacent teams: the customer console, execution limits, and access control live elsewhere; you own the data and mechanics they rely on.

 - Establish clear success measures and keep the squad accountable for outcomes, not only delivery.

 - Systems and data-model depth: You can design or critique an entity model, reason about reconciliation and idempotency in a sync, read an API contract, and explain why two systems reading the same events end up with different numbers.

 - Attention to detail: You know that if the billing data is wrong, everything built on it inherits the error, and you sequence work accordingly.

 - Prioritization under ambiguity: You make trade-offs explicit and connect foundational or data-quality work to commercial outcomes.

 - Ownership and autonomy: You grab problems without being asked, fix what you see broken, and drive outcomes without waiting for direction.

 - Exceptional communication: You're equally at home with engineers, the Finance team, and Sales, and you can make billing trade-offs legible to all of them.

 - Enterprise reality: You understand what self-hosted, air-gapped, and OEM deployments mean for licensing and metering.



Nice-to-haves

 - Usage-based billing: You've owned usage-based or hybrid (subscription plus usage) billing.

 - Vendor billing stacks: You've worked hands-on with Paddle, Stripe, Chargebee, Zuora or similar, and know where they break at enterprise contract volume.

 - Migration experience: You've run a billing-provider migration.

 - Hands-on ability: You can read code, query data, or prototype, even if you're not shipping it.

 - CRM integration: You've worked on Salesforce or CRM-to-billing integrations.

 - Domain familiarity: You know workflow automation, agent orchestration, or open-source / developer-community products.

 - Writing culture: You default to writing things down to create clarity and alignment.



Why join us?



At n8n, you'll be in the middle of the AI revolution. The shift from deterministic automation to agent autonomy is a genuinely open design space, and n8n has a credible claim to owning it. We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.


STAFF PLATFORM ENGINEER, AGENTIC ENGINEERING

Developer Productivity · AI Coding Agents · Developer Platform

Our ambition: an engineering organisation where humans and agents work as one continuously learning system, turning frontier AI capabilities and real-world feedback into more ambitious product development. We want n8n to be the reference for how this is done, without compromising quality, resilience or trust. Your main goal is to make that real.



This is a Staff individual contributor role in Developer Platform and the technical driving force behind ACDC (Agent-centric Development Cycle), our engineering-wide initiative for agentic development. Nobody has a playbook for this yet. You'll write ours.



You won't start from zero. Agents wired into Linear already automate around 80% of the development cycle on one of our developer platform projects, alongside pilots for insight, feature-flag and PR-review agents and a shared agent harness. Your job is to take this from promising experiments to the way n8n builds software.



This role is for someone who thinks about this problem constantly. You run agents all day, rebuild your own workflow every time the frontier moves, and have more ideas than time. 



You'll stay hands-on, building the first versions yourself, and shape how the work grows beyond one person.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


SET DIRECTION AND OWN THE OUTCOME

 - Identify where agentic development can make the greatest difference, using developer feedback, existing experiments and engineering performance data.

 - Set the strategy and priorities across agent execution, repository readiness, CI, security and developer workflows.

 - Make build, buy or pass decisions on tools and vendors, and own the cost and value trade-offs, including AI spend.

 - Make decisions where requirements are incomplete and the trade-offs between autonomy, reliability, security and review effort are still emerging.

 - Build alignment through technical proposals, clear decisions and working software, and report progress and impact to engineering leadership.


BUILD THE FOUNDATIONS

 - Design and build isolated execution environments where agents can work with the right access to code, tools and context, without exposing secrets or sensitive systems.

 - Own the safety model: which task categories agents may attempt, what they must never touch, and where human review is required, partnering with Security on sensitive areas like auth, billing, permissions and data handling.

 - Make n8n's monorepo agent-ready, working with Architecture and senior engineers on repo structure, testability, boundaries and the context agents need.


INTEGRATE AGENTS INTO HOW WE WORK

 - Build repeatable workflows that take Linear issues through agent execution, self-verification and review to merged PRs, across a growing range of task types.

 - Integrate agentic workflows with GitHub, CI, test infrastructure and code review, so the agentic path becomes the easiest path for engineers.

 - Extend the loop beyond coding: connect earlier signals like product research and customer requests, and later ones like production metrics, so agents contribute across the whole cycle.

 - Open it up beyond engineering, so PMs, designers and others can turn a well-defined issue into a reviewed, mergeable change.

 - Shape review practices, such as PR evidence that shows what changed, what ran, what risks remain and where human judgment is needed.


MEASURE WHAT WORKS

 - Build benchmarks from real historical engineering tasks to evaluate output quality, failure modes, review burden and production risk.

 - Define and track quality and adoption signals, such as reviewer acceptance rate, CI pass rate, rework rate and developer satisfaction.

 - Use data and feedback to change course, retire what doesn't work, and build trust across engineering.

 - 🧭 Staff-scope ownership: You’ve led complex platform, DevEx or engineering productivity initiatives across teams, from defining the problem to sustained adoption and measurable impact, where there was no established approach to follow.

 - 🤖 Agentic depth: You use coding agents daily as a power user, and you've built infrastructure around them, such as repo context and instructions, tool or MCP integrations, sandboxed execution or agent workflows in CI, that other engineers rely on.

 - 🎯 Product mindset for internal platforms: You treat engineers as your customers. You start from real friction, prioritise by impact, make build-vs-buy calls, weigh cost against value, and let adoption tell you whether something works.

 - 🤝 Direction without authority: You've set technical direction that multiple teams followed, through proposals, design reviews and credibility with senior engineers across Platform, Product Engineering, AI, Security and Architecture.

 - 🔐 Safety judgment: You've made real decisions on permissions, secrets, sandboxing, sensitive code paths and human-in-the-loop review, and can explain the trade-offs.

 - 📊 Measurement that drives decisions: You've built evaluations, benchmarks or quality metrics and used them to change course or retire things that didn't work. You care about outcomes, not lines of AI-generated code.

 - ✍️ Writing that changes decisions: Your technical proposals and documentation have shifted what teams did.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - 📦 TypeScript monorepos: You have worked in a large TypeScript, Node.js or JavaScript monorepo.

 - ⚙️ Developer platforms: You have experience with GitHub Actions, Linear, test infrastructure, preview environments or internal developer platforms.

 - 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Growing a team: You've mentored engineers or helped shape a new team as an initiative grew beyond one person.

 - 🌍 Open-source communities: You have contributed to open-source or source-available projects with active developer communities.

 - 🏢 B2B SaaS context: You understand environments where reliability, permissions, data handling and customer trust are central.

 - 🔗 Workflow automation: You're familiar with workflow automation, integration platforms, AI orchestration or developer-facing products.




WHY JOIN US?

At n8n, you'll define how autonomous AI agents become a trusted part of engineering inside one of Europe's fastest-growing AI-native infrastructure companies. title: Technical Customer Success Manager - EMEA
description:
ABOUT POSTHOG

PostHog is your product’s context layer. It ingests and stores your analytics, errors, replays, and business data so you and your agents can query and act on it.

We launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort https://posthog.com/handbook/story. We've since shipped more than a dozen products, including:

 - A suite of analytics and observability tools, including product analytics https://posthog.com/product-analytics, replay vision https://posthog.com/replay-vision, AI observability https://posthog.com/ai-observability, and error tracking https://posthog.com/error-tracking

 - PostHog MCP https://posthog.com/mcp for users and their agents to query and act on their product and business data

 - Data warehouse https://posthog.com/context-warehouse/managed-warehouse so users can query product and customer data together using custom SQL insights.

We are:

 1. Product-led. More than 500K organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit.

 2. Default alive https://paulgraham.com/aord.html. Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.

 3. Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey.

We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible https://posthog.com/deskhog. 

 


THINGS WE CARE ABOUT

 - Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook https://posthog.com/handbook. Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.

 - Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams https://posthog.com/handbook/wide-company and make product decisions https://posthog.com/handbook/which-products. Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.

 - Shipping fast: Why not now? https://posthog.com/handbook/values#why-not-now We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers https://posthog.com/founders/cracked-manifesto who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.

 - Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days https://posthog.com/handbook/company/culture#were-on-the-makers-schedule, and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had.

 - Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy https://posthog.com/deskhog with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun.


WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A customer-obsessed person to take care of a large number of our larger customers. You’ll engage with them regularly to ensure their continued retention and growth.

 - You'll need to be incredibly helpful, technical enough to help our customers, and solve real problems without asking a sales engineer for help. 

 - No going away and asking an expert by default. You will be the expert!

 - You’re great at building relationships with customers, understanding their priorities, and ensuring they are set up for success both today and in the long term.

 - We do not care what your old job title was. We care that you want to talk to customers, own the relationship and help them get more from PostHog.
   
   - Some of our best TCSMs used to ship code. Now they ship happy customers. Ex-dev, ex-TAM, ex-something-else? All good if you are technical and want to own customers, not just be near them!




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

You’ll be the face of PostHog for anywhere from 25-40 paying customers in the $20k-$100k+ ARR range. Some of these customers will have come through our sales process and be well-known to us, while others will have self-served and never talked to us before! 

It'll be your responsibility to ensure that both types of customers stay with us. That means taking care of the technical side (debugging, config advice), the commercial side (pricing questions, credit renewals), and the human side (multi-threading, managing escalations).

Day to day, it looks like:

 - Building relationships with your users. You should know who the key people are at each company, and they should know you. 

 - Owning their feedback and making sure it gets to the wider PostHog team.

 - Investigating technical issues. You're the first person to dig into customer issues, often solving them yourself rather than immediately passing them to support.

 - Being super responsive to their Slack messages, support tickets, and emails.

 - Being their favorite ever Customer Success person to work with!

More broadly, you'll watch product usage and revenue data so customer health doesn't move into the red, and act early when it does. Your aim is to never be surprised when a customer tells us they are leaving. If you want to build automations to help you do your job here, go for it!

Interesting reads:

 - Tyler's blog to see what a day as a TCSM looks like! https://posthog.com/blog/customer-success-at-posthog 

 - Ryan's blog for an engineer's view into the world of customer-facing work https://posthog.com/blog/being-in-a-sales-role-has-made-me-a-better-software-engineer

 - Julia's blog on hiring for this role https://posthog.com/blog/hiring-technical-csms

This role comprises a base salary component, plus a bonus https://posthog.com/handbook/cs-and-onboarding/how-we-work#how-contractual-bonus-works---technical-csms for hitting/exceeding customer retention targets. The salary in our compensation calculator is the OTE (80/20). 




WHAT YOU WON’T BE DOING

❌  Taking someone with you to every customer meeting. It’ll normally be you and the customer. Very occasionally, you might bring a product engineer with you, e.g. if they are one of our first customers paying for a new product. 

❌  Aggressively pursuing expansion opportunities. This role is primarily focused on retention. 




REQUIREMENTS

 - Technically capable. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable working with code. You troubleshoot issues customers run into (and sometimes even raise PRs yourself to fix bugs) and advise on configuration best practices across all PostHog products. 

 - You get how product teams work. You know the roles, how they collaborate, and how they ship features - so you can help them use PostHog to solve real problems. For example, why running experiments matters, how to use product analytics and session replay together to find drop-off points and test fixes, or when error tracking helps teams ship better.

 - Strong customer focus. You need to help our users and remove any blockers to them using PostHog effectively – not route them elsewhere and move on.

 - Able to work at scale. You'll have around 40 customers. You can't treat them all the same, and you won't try to.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience working with similar technologies, i.e. developer tools more broadly, or specifically product analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, data warehouses, or data pipelines.

 - You’ve been in a Pre-sales or Technical Account Manager role before, bringing both technical expertise and commercial acumen.

If you have a disability, please let us know if there's any way we can make the interview process better for you - we're happy to accommodate! 

#LI-DNI

title: Senior / Staff Fullstack Engineer
description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

As a small team, we’re all generalists and constantly picking up new challenges. When it comes to code, we’re looking to work with experienced people who can pick a problem and solve it.  We use TypeScript and build scalable systems so we can continuously make progress on a solid foundation. We don’t expect you to have a background in everything we use, but we do expect strong JavaScript fundamentals and a background working with React and TypeScript.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America and Europe. You can work from most timezones within these regions. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you'll do

 - Build new user-facing features with everything from database models to GraphQL resolvers and UI components

 - Optimize our data synchronization stack by applying better serialization protocols

 - Add real-time collaborative editing to our content editor

 - Improve performance by profiling and tweaking virtualized list rendering

 - Add analytics, monitoring, and alerts to our service so that we can better respond to operational incidents

 - Open-source any non-trivial innovations that come out of our work on the product

 - Redefine best-in-class software development processes so that we can build a purpose-built product.

What we're looking for

 - 5+ years of experience building customer-facing products at a high-quality software company

 - Strong React and TypeScript fundamentals, with experience across the full stack (Browser technologies, Node, GraphQL, PostgreSQL)

 - Track record of driving complex, end-to-end features (not just incremental improvements and refactors) with visible impact on the product

 - Product sensibility: you care about UX, speed, and polish, and you push back when something doesn't feel right

 - Comfortable working without heavy PM overhead; you can help to shape the problem, not just implement a solution

 - High ownership mentality: self-directed, full-lifecycle builder who takes a feature from idea to shipped

 - Thrives in a remote, async-first environment with a lean, high-output team

 - Experience at a startup or a company with a genuinely high engineering bar

Our tech

This stack reflects the systems we build and operate. You’re not expected to have experience with everything listed, but you should be excited to work close to product, performance, and real-world scale.

 - Agentic workload system utilizing temporal, operating at production scale

 - Proprietary websocket data sync framework built for speed and offline support

 - React, MobX, styled-components on the frontend

 - Extensive, widely used, GraphQL API and SDK

 - Node, Postgres, Temporal, and Redis in the backend

 - Hosted on Google Cloud with k8s

 - GitHub, Slack, Notion

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms including early exercise in the US and extended exercise windows

 - Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

 - Paid co-working space or desk

 - Health coverage (based on country requirements)

 - 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

 - 4 months paid parental leave

 - Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

 - Regular team events and off-sites

 - Remote-first with no required commute

Learn how we think and work

 - Our hiring process: How we hire at Linear https://linear.app/now/how-we-hire-at-linear

 - How we work: Designing remote work at Linear https://linear.app/now/designing-remote-work-at-linear

 - Why and how we do work trials https://linear.app/blog/why-and-how-we-do-work-trials-at-linear  Linear blog post

 - How we use AI in design https://designerfund.substack.com/p/ai-design-linear feature of Linear's design team

 - Scaling our real-time sync engine https://linear.app/blog/scaling-the-linear-sync-engine  talk by our cofounder, Tuomas Artman, at Linear's 2023 offsite

 - Our recent tender offer: Sharing Linear’s growth with the people building it https://linear.app/now/sharing-growth-with-the-people-building-linear

title: Product Manager
description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

We're looking for a senior to staff level Product Manager to join the team.

In this role, you'll be responsible for leading the development of products end-to-end, from conception through development and rollout. If you're excited to have a lot of ownership while remaining in the details day to day, this might be a great fit for you.

Linear is a product-led company that focuses on both building and selling. It's up to you to bring together the building and selling sides of the company in order to create something that our customers will love.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America or Europe time zones. You can work from anywhere within those regions. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you'll do

 - Perform up-front discovery through user interviews, competitive research, data analysis, etc. and present findings to the team with conviction and rigor

 - Help engineers and designers deeply understand user needs, empowering them to make great product decisions

 - Craft messaging around upcoming features that resonates with users

 - Enable sales and marketing teams to effectively communicate with and win with customers

What we’re looking for

 - 6+ years experience in the software industry

 - Previous experience in engineering and/or design roles

 - Exceptional product and operational judgement

 - World-class design & product taste

 - Shameless curiosity, a propensity to question things deeply

 - Extreme speed and clarity

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms including early exercise in the US and extended exercise windows

 - Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

 - Paid co-working space or desk

 - Health coverage (based on country requirements)

 - 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

 - 4 months paid parental leave

 - Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

 - Regular team events and off-sites

 - Remote-first with no required commute

Compensation

For US-based candidates, the expected cash compensation range for this role is $204,000—$252,000. For sales roles, this range represents on-target earnings (OTE), including base salary and variable compensation; for all other roles, it represents base salary. Final compensation is determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. For sales roles, actual earnings vary based on sales performance. Equity is a meaningful part of all offers at Linear.

title: Developer Relations
description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Linear is becoming a much broader product than people realize. With agents, mobile workflows, and new modalities, there’s a growing gap between what Linear can do and what people think it can do. This role exists to close that gap.

We’re looking for someone who will live inside the product, discover what’s possible, and show the world. That means figuring out the most compelling use cases for Linear’s AI agent, demonstrating real workflows that teams can adopt, and getting those stories out through whatever format works best, whether that’s a tweet, a video, a blog post, or a live demo at a conference. The goal is to help people understand what they can actually do with Linear and make that feel concrete and exciting.

Think of it as a product-obsessed marketer who is genuinely technical and knows how to communicate with depth.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in the US and Europe. You can work from anywhere within those regions. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you’ll do

 - Deeply understand Linear’s product, especially our AI agent and newer capabilities, and continuously discover productive, real-world use cases that teams would care about

 - Create content that demonstrates those use cases, whether that’s short-form social, blog posts, video walkthroughs, or live demos. Format follows the story, not the other way around

 - Build relationships with engineering and product-focused creators and collaborate on content that feels authentic rather than sponsored

 - Work with our video team to produce technical product content that comes across with genuine depth

 - Partner with support, sales, and product on developer-facing documentation and educational content

 - Stay plugged into the conversations happening on X, in newsletters, and at events, and make sure Linear has a voice in the ones that matter

What we’re looking for

 - Someone technical. You get code, understand how software gets built, and can talk about it credibly

 - Deep product intuition. You’re the kind of person who picks up a tool and immediately starts exploring what’s possible. You think in workflows and use cases rather than features

 - Comfortable on camera and on stage. You can demo a product, record a walkthrough, or speak at a conference without it feeling forced.

 - Twitter/X smart. You know how to use the platform, you understand what’s interesting to the people we’re trying to reach, and you can participate in the conversation with credibility

 - Curious and self-directed. You’re already finding the next interesting thing to talk about on your own, already following the right people and noticing the opportunities

 - Able to create video content end to end. You should be able to script, record, and edit a product walkthrough or demo without needing to hand it off to someone else

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms including early exercise in the US and extended exercise windows

 - Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

 - Paid co-working space or desk

 - Health coverage (based on country requirements)

 - 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

 - Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

 - Remote-first with no required commute

title: Field Marketing Manager, Europe
description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Field marketing at Linear is just getting started. Its job is to put us in front of the right people in the right room: executive dinners, conferences, partner events, and programs built with our Customer team around named accounts.

We're hiring our first Field Marketing Manager in Europe to take that motion from strategy to execution. You'll own the executive dinner calendar across cities, decide which third-party events and partner programs are worth our time, and build the invitations and follow-up that help our sellers turn a good evening into a real conversation. This is a hands-on role. You'll tap your venue and vendor network, build the run of show for each program, and be on site to run it.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in Europe, with London preferred. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel. This role involves frequent travel for events, including evenings.

What you’ll do

 - Own the executive dinner calendar across cities: pick the city, the venue, the date, and the theme for each dinner

 - Build each guest list with our Customer team, equip sellers with invitation sequences, and track RSVPs so every seat goes to someone worth having there

 - Manage venues and vendors, negotiate menus and minimums, and keep per-dinner spend, contracts, and travel logistics within budget

 - Brief our hosts and executives on who's attending and what we want to learn, be on site to run the night, and hand follow-ups to Sales afterward

 - Evaluate conferences and sponsorship offers by audience quality, account coverage, and expected return, then plan how we show up: booth or no booth, side dinners, customer meetings, and speaking slots

 - Co-host dinners, workshops, and meetups with partners, and agree up front on guest lists, costs, and who follows up

 - Sit with Sales each quarter to pick target accounts, build lightweight formats an AE can request for a key account, and report on attendance, meetings held, pipeline influenced, and feedback from attendees and account owners

What we’re looking for

 - 3+ years in field marketing, event marketing, or B2B events, ideally at a software company. Experience in developer tools, SaaS, or another technical product is a plus

 - A track record of running dinners, roundtables, or other small-format events end to end, plus experience planning around conferences: sponsorships, side events, and customer meetings

 - Experience working next to Sales. You know how to build a target account list, get an AE to care about an event, and tell them afterward what happened

 - Strong project management. You can run several cities and events at once without dropping details

 - Comfort with budgets, vendor contracts, and a spreadsheet. Hands-on time with HubSpot and event attribution is a plus

 - Clear writing and an easy way with senior guests, hosts, and partners. Experience marketing to engineering and product leaders is a bonus

 - Experience building an event series from the ground up, including a playbook someone else could run

 - Willingness to travel often, including evenings

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms

 - Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

 - Paid co-working space or desk

 - Health coverage (based on country requirements)

 - 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

 - 4 months paid parental leave

 - Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

 - Regular team events and off-sites
