description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Developer Support Engineer to help developers get the most out of RevenueCat, from their first integration to their next pricing experiment. You’ll work directly with customers every day, on anything from a quick question to a deep investigation in their apps, and every problem you solve gets a developer back to shipping and earning. You’ll also work with Engineering and Product, turning what you learn into better docs, clearer bug reports and a better product for every developer on RevenueCat.


ABOUT YOU:

 - You have 3+ years of experience in an engineering or technical role.

 - You have experience integrating and shipping RevenueCat in a mobile app.

 - You have an understanding of the mobile development and release process.

 - You have experience in either iOS (Swift / Objective-C) or Android (Java / Kotlin)

 - You have great debugging skills: You will be identifying why apps aren’t working, often with limited information.

 - You have experience debugging code issues utilizing stack traces.

 - You have an interest in "wearing many hats," doing what it takes to help developers every day.

 - You have excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills: You will be writing to, presenting to and speaking with developers and colleagues daily.

 - You have empathy for developers and their development/learning process: we usually hear from developers at their lowest and need to be understanding.

 - You have a demonstrated creative problem-solving approach and strong analytical skills.


IN THE FIRST MONTH, YOU'LL:

 - Learn the common frustrations our customers have, and help them get unblocked to ship their apps

 - Learn the internal tools and processes used by the support team

 - Make improvements to our docs and support articles based on customer interactions to reduce support

 - Work with our engineering team to untangle complex tickets


WITHIN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Make product suggestions that will improve the developer experience and reduce support

 - Build internal apps to test and reproduce issues

 - Work directly with customers to assist with onboarding and solution engineering


WITHIN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Identify key problem areas for developers and make targeted improvements that help developers

 - Improve and create internal tools and dashboards for support and other internal processes

 - Make significant contributions to the support process that helps you and your teammates be more efficient


WITHIN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Develop a super-hero like intuition for the root causes of tickets and become an expert troubleshooter

 - Interview, hire and mentor additional support engineers

 - Discover new and unexpected ways to delight developers with our support experience


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

 - 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

 - A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

 - Paid desk at a co-working space

 - Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend


INTERVIEWING AT REVENUECAT

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/company/how-we-hire-at-revenuecat/, including tips to help you succeed.

title: Senior Data Scientist, Product
description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

We are looking for a Senior Product Data Scientist who is deeply product-minded and highly proactive.

This is not a role for someone who waits for perfectly defined questions or works in isolation. We are looking for someone who actively looks at our data, understands our customers’ pain points, identifies opportunities, and pushes ideas forward.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, and Analytics to shape what we build, why we build it, and how we measure success. Your work will directly power customer-facing features such as LTV prediction, experimentation and statistical significance, benchmarking, and entirely new data-driven products we have not built yet.

You will be expected to bring ideas to the table, backed by analysis and clear hypotheses, and to influence product direction through data.

Our data stack includes a Python backend, PostgreSQL production databases, Snowflake, dbt, and AWS.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Proactively explore RevenueCat’s data to identify customer problems, opportunities, and product bets.

 - Translate ambiguous product and business problems and questions into clear analyses, models, and recommendations.

 - Partner with Product Managers to shape roadmaps, not just execute on them.

 - Design, build, and ship production-grade predictive and descriptive models that power customer-facing features.

 - Define and evaluate statistical approaches for experimentation, benchmarking, and forecasting.

 - Communicate insights clearly and persuasively to technical and non-technical audiences, with a focus on customer impact.

 - Continuously iterate on shipped models and features based on real-world usage and feedback.

This role has real ownership. You will not just support decisions, you will help drive them.


ABOUT YOU

You are a Senior Data Scientist who cares deeply about impact and product outcomes.

From a skills perspective, you bring:

 - 5+ years of experience working as a Data Scientist.

 - Strong SQL skills and comfort with data modeling.

 - Experience building and deploying predictive and descriptive models in production.

 - Experience writing or collaborating on production-ready Python code.

 - A solid understanding of statistics and experimentation, ideally including Bayesian approaches.

 - The ability to clearly explain complex ideas and results to broad audiences.

You recognize yourself in several of these:

 - You are highly proactive and opinionated, and you are comfortable pushing ideas forward.

 - You enjoy working with messy, real-world data and imperfect information.

 - You care more about creating customer value than academic elegance.

 - You are comfortable operating in ambiguity and building structure where none exists.

 - You enjoy working closely with Product teams and influencing decisions.

 - You are excited by the consumer subscription ecosystem and curious about how developers make money.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE


IN THE FIRST MONTH, YOU'LL:

 - Understand our data models.

 - Get to know the team.

 - Ramp up on the ongoing data feature work.

 - Implement and ship your first project.


WITHIN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Meaningfully contribute to shipping a data feature to thousands of developers.

 - Work with our Product, Analytics and Engineering teams to improve our data pipelines for data science features.

 - Launch your own explorations into our data to fulfill your own curiosity.


WITHIN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Own one or more core data-powered features end to end.

 - Influence the data feature roadmap with clear, data-backed proposals.

 - Be a go-to partner for product teams on data-driven decision making.


WITHIN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Propose and lead entirely new data-driven product initiatives.

 - Push the boundaries of how RevenueCat uses data to help developers grow revenue.

 - Help shape how data science operates at RevenueCat as the function grows.


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

 - 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

 - A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

 - Paid desk at a co-working space

 - Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

description:

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join the team working on analytics features in RevenueCat.

RevenueCat is the monetization engine for 40% of new subscription apps shipped — and the number of apps shipped is growing exponentially. We are uniquely positioned not only to give individual developer impactful information into the performance of their own apps, but also deliver truly unique data and insight given our position in the market; we know what good looks like, and we can not only put numbers in context, but give specific recommendations on metrics to target, experiments to run and anomalies to investigate.

Our analytics features help app developers make better decisions that improve the monetization of their apps. As product manager on this team, you are responsible for working with your team to set the vision and roadmap, delivering on it, launching new functionality, and increasing the impact of the team.

This role requires:

 - being technical to understand how our analytics system works and its constraint

 - being analytical to be able to define how to show data as well as debugging issues and edge cases

 - being customer obsessed to understand what information app developers need for their decisions and how we can provide this information to them

 - having an understanding of the app ecosystem, how the economics of app businesses work, and what success means for app developers

You will oversee all of the Analytics features at RevenueCat — our charts, benchmarking, dashboard, and predictive LTV. You'll partner directly with leadership, collaborate across engineering and data teams, and act as the primary driver for how our customers understand and grow their revenue.


ABOUT YOU

Skills & Experience

 - You have 5+ years of product management or adjacent experience, with meaningful time shipping complex products.

 - You’re analytical. You can’t do your job without data platform access. You are proficient in SQL (or similar tools) — whatever tool you need to know, you’ll learn. You love diving deep into data yourself. You’re experienced in developing robust and scalable metrics.

 - You are technical. Coding is not a core requirement for this role, being able to prototype with code is (using your preferred AI stack). You can deeply understand how RevenueCat works — what is simple and what is complex within our domain. Maybe you haven’t built and shipped a mobile app yourself (yet) but you have enough knowledge to work closely and independently with highly technical folks. You can discuss APIs, data models, and risk logic with engineering partners and enjoy diving into system details

 - You’re an excellent communicator. You can express complex ideas clearly and succinctly — written and verbal, synchronous and asynchronous, across timezones and mediums. You can get your point across.

Values and Abilities

 - You act like an owner. You roll up your sleeves, dive into the logs, and get something done yourself.

 - You thrive in ambiguity. You are comfortable making low-information, high-stakes decisions. You can quickly get to confidence, move on, and iterate.

 - You're a systems thinker. You can step back from a specific customer request and see the broader system. You build things that scale.

 - You're deep on the details. You care about what users experience, not just what the data says.

 - You know when it's good enough. You are obsessed with getting things right, but you know when you're at diminishing returns. You have a bias toward shipping. You love building — and are energized by discovery, experimentation, and rapid iteration.

 - You’re passionate about great data visualization. Chart sins grind your gears. Your visualizations deliver meaningful insights. You care what is says — and what it looks like — and you know those things are dependent on each other.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product strategy and roadmap for RevenueCat's Analytics products.

 - Be obsessed with your customers. You will triage and investigate complex data and analytics problems deeply, instead of fully delegating to engineering. Dig deep to understand what developers really want — distill signal from noise and good ideas from bad ones.

 - Recommend, develop and maintain new benchmarks and metrics that deliver value to our developers, and help them make more money. Be the go-to person when a number looks off.

 - Set the vision. Create a plan that is cohesive, intentional, and impactful. Break that down into meaningful chunks on a reasonable timeline.

 - Get it done. Collaborate closely with engineering, data science, and GTM teams to bring robust analytics and experimentation tools to market. This job can not be done alone, and will require deep understanding of the individual products and the infrastructure that hooks them together.

The salary for this role is $230,000 USD. You can view our full Compensation Philosophy here https://www.notion.so/revenuecat/RevenueCat-Compensation-Philosophy-82b57cae23ab4c9bb62dfe4e933d32d0 for additional details.

In the first month, you'll:

 - Get to know the product, customers, and team

 - Contribute to shipping a meaningful feature to thousands of developers

 - Be ramped up on ongoing projects in your teams

Within the first 3 months, you'll:

 - Have formed a strong working relationship with your engineering manager and design counterpart

 - Have taken ownership of the roadmap and prioritization for your team (jointly with the engineering manager)

 - Work with your engineering manager and leadership to define quarterly objectives for your teams

 - Have shipped the first bigger feature end to end

 - Work with your team to discover opportunities and solutions to deliver value to our customers

 - Play an integral role in your team’s discovery and delivery processes

 - Understand the fundamentals of our tech stack and its complexities, and drive the evaluation feasibility/value tradeoffs in collaboration with your teams

Within the first 6 months, you'll:

 - Have helped your team grow and become a high-performing, engaged team in line with our company values

 - Effectively collaborate with internal stakeholders of all levels

 - Be an expert of your areas of the product and the related customer needs, and instill customer empathy in your teams

 - Independently drive all product-related decisions in your area

 - Have contributed meaningfully to our knowledge of our customers and their needs, our industry, and important trends

 - Develop a longer term vision for your area of the product in line with the product strategy

 - Work with your teams to improve processes and interfaces with other teams

Within the first 12 months, you'll:

 - Be ready to kill something you have shipped if we learned it didn't deliver the value we hoped

 - Explore completely new opportunities for how RevenueCat may provide greater value to our customers

 - Make meaningful contributions to our overall product strategy

 - Have delivered a material, business-impacting new benefit to our customers in your product area


WHAT WE OFFER:

title: Senior CRO Designer, Paywalls and Funnels
description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


ABOUT THE TEAM

You’ll join a cross‑functional group of app monetization subject matter experts who partner directly with RevenueCat customers and prospects. As part of the broader Customer Growth org, this team designs and implements high‑impact paywalls, onboarding flows, and purchase funnels using RevenueCat’s no‑code builders and experimentation tools, then feeds learnings back into our product, templates, and educational content

You’ll also collaborate closely with our content, marketing, and advocacy teams to turn real‑world project outcomes into templates, case studies, webinars, and best‑practice guides for the broader app community


ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior CRO Designer, Paywalls & Funnels, you’ll be the person RevenueCat customers trust when the question is: “How do we get more users to convert and stay subscribed?”

You will:

 - Design & build high‑converting paywalls and funnels
   
   - Use RevenueCat’s paywall and experiment builders to design, configure, and ship paywalls, onboarding flows, upgrade paths, and win‑back experiences for mobile apps across categories
   
   - Translate brands and product value props into clear, compelling paywall layouts, messaging, and pricing presentations
     

 - Lead conversion optimization projects for customers and prospects
   
   - Run structured discovery with customers and prospects to understand their business model, audience, and constraints
   
   - Propose experiment plans (e.g., value prop framing, pricing presentation, trial vs. no‑trial, placement and timing of paywalls)
   
   - Partner with apps to launch multivariate tests and interpret results, using RevenueCat’s analytics and experimentation tooling
     

 - Codify patterns into reusable assets
   
   - Distill what’s working across projects into reusable templates, checklists, and patterns that can be implemented directly in RevenueCat’s builders
   
   - Work with Product to inform our paywall components, presets, and default templates
     

 - Create educational content with Advocacy & Marketing
   
   - Collaborate with Growth Advocacy and Content teams to turn your project learnings into:
     
     - Example paywalls and funnel templates
     
     - Blog posts, guides, and best‑practice documentation
     
     - Webinars, live reviews, and conference talks or workshops
   
   - Participate in public‑facing sessions (e.g., teardown streams, office hours) as a visible expert on monetization UX
     

 - Champion monetization UX best practices
   
   - Advise Sales, Customer Success, and Support on paywall and funnel best practices they can bring into customer conversations
   
   - Provide feedback to Product & Engineering on how practitioners use our builders in the wild, highlighting opportunities for new features, components, and workflows


ABOUT YOU

You’re a conversion‑focused designer who lives at the intersection of mobile product design, growth, and experimentation. You have a track record of shipping real paywalls and funnels that move business metrics, not just portfolios

You have:

 - Deep hands‑on experience with paywalls & funnels
   
   - 5–8+ years designing consumer mobile experiences, with a substantial portion spent on subscription or purchase flows (e.g., paywalls, onboarding, upgrade/upsell, win‑back, account limits)
   
   - Experience either:
     
     - At a mobile app studio / product team owning monetization UX, or
     
     - At an agency/consultancy repeatedly designing and optimizing paywalls and funnels for multiple apps
       

 - Strong conversion & experimentation mindset
   
   - Comfort defining hypotheses, success metrics, and test plans (e.g., CVR, trial start rate, activation, LTV)
   
   - Experience using analytics and experimentation tools to interpret results and iterate quickly
   
   - Ability to balance conversion gains with long‑term user trust and platform guidelines
     

 - Mobile‑first product design skills
   
   - Excellent interaction and visual design chops for small screens and high‑stakes surfaces (like paywalls and purchase flows)
   
   - Strong UX writing instincts for concise, value‑focused copy and pricing messaging
   
   - Proficiency in modern design tools (e.g. Figma) and comfort translating designs into no‑code builder configurations
     

 - Customer‑facing communication skills
   
   - Confidence leading workshops, design reviews, and strategy sessions with customers and prospects
   
   - Ability to present options, pros/cons, and trade‑offs to both designers and non‑design stakeholders (founders, PMs, marketers)
   
   - Great written communication for async collaboration in a remote team
     

 - Values & ways of working
   
   - You’re energized by our mission to help developers make more money
   
   - You work iteratively and ship value quickly rather than waiting for perfection
   
   - You have an ownership mentality: You see broken or unclear experiences and feel compelled to improve them
   
   - You’re comfortable working in a fully remote, distributed team and collaborating across time zones

In your first month, you’ll:

 - Learn RevenueCat’s products, especially paywalls, experiments, and analytics

 - Join customer calls to understand our process and common challenges

 - Audit a handful of existing customer paywalls and funnels and build your first recommendations

Within 3 months, you’ll:

 - Own several customer projects end‑to‑end, from discovery through experiment analysis

 - Ship multiple paywall and funnel variations using RevenueCat’s builders

 - Partner with Advocacy/Content on at least one public asset (template, blog post, teardown, or webinar segment)

Within 6 months, you’ll:

 - Be the go‑to expert internally for monetization UX, paywall patterns, and funnel optimization

 - Maintain and evolve an internal “playbook” of best practices and tested patterns

 - Influence the roadmap for our paywall and experiment tooling based on patterns you see across customers

Within 12 months, you’ll:

 - Have materially improved conversion for a portfolio of customer apps, with clear before/after stories

 - Help define our strategy for paywall templates and monetization UX guidance at scale

 - Represent RevenueCat in public‑facing educational content (webinars, AMAs, workshops, or conference talks) as a leading voice on mobile monetization UX

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

title: Sales & Operations Specialist, RC Capital
description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

RC Capital is RevenueCat's first move into financial services. Our first product, Early Payouts, gives developers access to App Store proceeds without waiting the usual 30 to 60 days for Apple and Google to pay them.

As Sales & Operations Specialist, RC Capital, you will own the customer lifecycle end-to-end - from identifying and qualifying suitable prospects through screening, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, account operations, and portfolio health. You will combine commercial judgment, customer care, operational discipline, and risk awareness to help RC Capital acquire and serve more healthy customers.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on a small founding team. You might move from a discovery call to an onboarding issue, a portfolio review, and a workflow improvement in the same day. You will work closely with Sales, Support, Product, Data, Finance, Legal, Marketing, and GTM Operations, and report to the VP of Strategy & Operations. You will also help build the playbook and systems future teammates inherit.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN:

 - Sales and qualification. Manage a portfolio of inbound and targeted outbound opportunities. Run discovery, assess product and customer fit, coordinate screening, handle objections, maintain momentum, and guide suitable prospects to a clear decision.

 - Onboarding and activation. Lead approved customers from decision to activated. Ensure customers understand how to use Early Payouts successfully.

 - Customer support and portfolio operations. Serve as a reliable point of contact for customers, including questions, disputes, and operational issues. Coordinate with RevenueCat Support and specialist teams, and own follow-through through resolution.

 - Risk-aware execution. Apply documented customer, fraud, and risk policies consistently; investigate issues; document decisions; monitor emerging patterns; and make sound recommendations. Escalate exceptions and regulated or high-impact decisions to the appropriate risk, legal, finance, or leadership owner.

 - Lifecycle performance and insight. Maintain a reliable view of pipeline, onboarding, support demand, usage, and portfolio health. Turn data into recommendations on funnel quality, conversion, time to activation, drop-off, retention, customer experience, and risk indicators. Bring structured customer insight to Product to inform roadmaps.

 - Systems, automation, and playbooks. Improve CRM, support workflows, internal handoffs, reporting, documentation, and automation. Use AI thoughtfully to reduce manual work and response times without weakening controls or customer trust. Partner with Marketing, Operations, Data, and Product on durable implementations.

 - Customer and growth. Partner with Marketing on focused acquisition and lifecycle experiments. Support marketing efforts like campaign execution, competitive analysis, and content that drives demand.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in a high-ownership, customer-facing commercial or operations role spanning sales, account management, customer success, customer support, or customer operations.

 - A track record of moving opportunities through a commercial process and managing a meaningful volume of customer relationships with strong follow-through.

 - Experience in fintech, payments, lending, factoring, embedded finance, or another environment where customer growth and operational risk are closely connected.

You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

We are looking for a Head of Sales to build and lead the commercial system that converts RevenueCat's market position, product signals, and customer demand into dependable revenue, regardless of that revenue coming in the form of an immediate contract, a self-serve credit-swipe, or long-term expansion.

In the ‘app monetization platform’ category, RevenueCat currently has about a 90% marketshare, ranging from the biggest apps in the world (ChatGPT, Ladder, VSCO) to a long tail of 100,000+ indies and startups vying to make it big. We only power roughly 25% of in-app revenue, though: The majority of apps still tries to build this themselves. Your job will be to show them the error of their ways. Not (just) to close a deal, but because we truly, deeply believe we will help them make more money.

As the Head of Sales, you’ll lead the AE and Sales Engineering teams, bringing both teams together in a single, well-oiled machine. You’ll set the functional strategy, develop talent, own forecasting and results, and you’ll personally help move important opportunities forward without becoming the required manager or closer on every deal.




WHY WE ARE HIRING FOR THIS ROLE NOW

We have more opportunities than the current team can consistently identify, prioritize and pursue.

Our reputation and market position produce consistent touch points with the majority of potential prospects, without those touch points turning into economic opportunities. At the same time, we’re rapidly expanding into new markets and product areas that need more proactive sales support than we can deliver.

We need a leader who can make several motions work together without forcing them into one generic process:

 - Complex evaluations involving technical, business, security, legal, and procurement stakeholders.

 - Faster mid-market opportunities that require strong qualification and commercial momentum.

 - Self-exploration where customer behavior reveals an opportunity before a formal handraise.

 - Carefully researched outbound engagement with app businesses where RevenueCat has a specific reason to be useful.

 - Partner-sourced and selected regional motions whose economics must be demonstrated before they are scaled.

The foundations exist: Account Executives, Sales Engineers, product and usage data, a respected brand, Growth Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Product, Finance, and Customer Growth. This role will turn those ingredients into a successful Sales function.




WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the function. Set goals, metrics, operating cadences, headcount plans, budget, organization design, executive communication, and the performance bar across Sales.

 - Build a multi-motion Sales system. Define how strategic, mid-market, product-led, outbound, partner, and regional opportunities are identified, qualified, staffed, and advanced, across a growing product portfolio.

 - Create qualified pipeline beyond inbound. Develop focused account and outbound programs grounded in customer evidence, specific use cases, market events, and product signals rather than undifferentiated prospecting.

 - Close the coverage gap. Ensure high-potential product usage, sign-ups, inbound requests, support interactions, and target-account signals quickly result in a named owner and an intentional next action.

 - Build the team. We have good building blocks in place but the team needs to be significantly expanded to take on our current scale. Hire and developer exception talent, and define what makes a great sales team member at RevenueCat.

 - Remain close to customers. Participate in customer conversations every week and personally lead or support opportunities with unusual economic, technical, or organizational complexity.

 - Make the forecast useful. Establish definitions and inspection habits that distinguish real, qualified opportunity value from incomplete records, existing usage conversions, renewals, total contract value, or loosely influenced demand.

 - Help shape pricing and packaging. Bring a clear Sales point of view to cross-functional pricing and packaging decisions, using customer evidence to advocate for structures that support value, adoption, and durable growth.

 - Get cross-functional collaboration right. Define how Sales works with Customer Growth, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, Revenue Operations, Product, Engineering, TAM, and Support without creating duplicate account ownership or executive rescue as the default operating model.

 - Create learning from every deal. Turn repeated discovery patterns, objections, migrations, wins, and losses into better playbooks, reusable assets, Product evidence, and team training.

We help even more apps make even more money, without turning Sales into the standard SaaS “spray and pray” factory

 - Success across multiple distinct motions such as strategic enterprise, mid-market, product-led Sales assistance, focused outbound, channel, or regional selling.

 - Experience creating qualified pipeline rather than depending entirely on inbound demand or a large SDR organization.

 - Enough product and technical fluency to talk to Engineering about a possible migration without relying on Sales Engineering for every conversation.

 - Fluency with pipeline inspection, forecasting, conversion data, capacity planning, and performance management.

 - Evidence of hiring, coaching, developing leaders, raising standards, and making difficult talent decisions.

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Finance, Operations, Partnerships, and post-sale teams.

 - A desire to stay personally engaged with customers and live commercial work as the organization grows (and an understanding of why this matters).


IDEALLY, YOU

 - Have worked in a product-led or usage-based business where self-service remains an important customer path.

 - Understand app infrastructure, payments, monetization, developer platforms, or another domain with meaningful implementation complexity.

 - Have built a productive Account Executive and Sales Engineering partnership.

 - Have experience with partner-sourced, international, or regional programs.

 - Have sold to buying groups spanning engineering, product, growth, finance, security, legal, and procurement.

The goal is not to give every customer the same high-touch service. It is to identify where RevenueCat can create disproportionate value, deploy the right kind of help, and turn every successful customer intervention into knowledge that benefits the rest of the customer base.

You will lead a multi-lane Customer Growth function spanning the CSM team, Growth Advisory, Growth Advocacy, and the emerging Customer Enablement function. For our highest-value customers, this means deep account context, growth diagnosis, stakeholder mapping, product-adoption strategy, technical-account coordination, and clear next-step ownership. For high-potential customers, it means identifying them early and providing the right help before revenue has fully materialized. For customers with specific growth bottlenecks, it means bringing in the right specialist. For the broader customer base, it means scalable education through Growth Advocates, lifecycle guidance, office hours, playbooks, templates, product nudges, and eventually dynamic next-best-action systems.

Your job is to make Customer Growth one operating system rather than a collection of disconnected activities.


WHY WE ARE HIRING FOR THIS ROLE NOW

RevenueCat serves tiny indie apps, fast-growing startups, games, media companies, health and fitness apps, AI products, marketplaces, and some of the most sophisticated consumer app businesses in the world.

The app market is top-heavy, so the human touch must be allocated deliberately. At the same time, a customer that is small today may become strategically important very quickly. Contract status and current revenue are necessary signals, but they are not sufficient.

We already have many of the ingredients: CSMs, a CSM Team Lead role, Growth Advocates, Customer Growth Advisory specialists, Product, Support, Marketing, Sales, TAM, Data, and one of the richest datasets in app monetization. We need a leader who can turn those ingredients into a coherent function.


WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own Customer Growth strategy across the full customer base. Define how RevenueCat helps customers grow after they begin using the product, including named accounts, high-potential customers, specialist-assisted customers, scaled customers, and the long tail.

 - Build segmentation and coverage. Use current value, future potential, adoption, intent, growth moments, risk, and strategic importance to decide who receives named CSM coverage, time-bound help, specialist advisory, scaled education, product-led guidance, or monitoring.

 - Lead through the CSM Team Lead. Set the bar for customer context, account strategy, stakeholder management, growth diagnosis, adoption planning, commercial awareness, and follow-through. Develop the Team Lead and create a strong leadership bench rather than becoming the permanent CSM manager.

 - Identify high-potential customers early. Work with Data, Product, Sales, Marketing, and Support to find customers with meaningful future potential before revenue alone makes them obvious.

 - Govern Growth Advisory. Define intake, qualification, expected impact, output quality, follow-through, and reuse. Specialists should be deployed against specific high-value problems rather than become general-purpose consulting capacity.

 - Make Growth Advocacy a customer-education channel. Ensure Growth Advocates turn real customer learning into authoritative one-to-many education for existing customers and the broader app ecosystem.

 - Build Customer Enablement and Scaled Growth. Create the roadmap for lifecycle programs, templates, office hours, documentation, automation, product nudges, and next-best-action guidance.

 - Drive meaningful product adoption. Partner with Product and Product Marketing so customers adopt RevenueCat capabilities in ways that help them win, rather than merely increasing feature activity.

 - Create clear cross-functional decision rights. Define how Customer Growth works with Sales, TAM, Support, Product, Marketing, and Data without turning CSMs into AEs, TAMs into a catch-all, or collaboration into meeting theater.

 - Build the customer-insight loop. Repeated customer questions should become product improvements, enablement, playbooks, benchmarks, documentation, lifecycle programs, and market education.

 - Own the function. Set metrics, operating cadences, headcount plans, budget, organization design, executive communication, and the talent bar across Customer Growth.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE


WITHIN THE FIRST MONTH

 - Meet directly with at least 15 customers across different sizes, growth stages, product footprints, and monetization models—including high-value, high-potential, at-risk, and scaled customers.

 - Take point on at least two live customer-growth situations. Work alongside the CSM, Advisory, TAM, Support, or Product partner to diagnose the problem, agree ownership, and move each customer to a concrete next milestone.

 - Ship at least one no-regrets improvement to a broken handoff, account motion, Advisory route, or customer experience rather than waiting for a complete strategy.

 - Establish a clear operating agreement with the CSM Team Lead and act on urgent customer, talent, or ownership issues.

 - Build a working view of the team, coverage, high-potential misses, lane boundaries, and metrics—deep enough to make decisions, without allowing analysis to delay action.


WITHIN THE FIRST THREE MONTHS

 - Act as executive sponsor for a small set of strategically important or high-potential customers and personally lead at least two customer-growth interventions through a measurable milestone.

 - Put the first version of segmentation and coverage into production on real accounts, then revise it from evidence.

 - Run decision-oriented account reviews and a working Growth Advisory intake and follow-through motion.

 - Ship the first scaled education or Customer Enablement program based on a repeated customer need.

 - Make the first material changes to ownership, operating cadence, or talent where the current model is not working.

 - Establish a customer-insight loop that turns frontline evidence into owned Product, education, lifecycle, or process actions.


WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS

 - Maintain direct customer contact every week and own selected executive relationships while leading the wider system through the CSM Team Lead and specialist leaders.

 - Operate a functioning multi-lane Customer Growth model with clear owners, live handoffs, and visible outcomes across CSM, Growth Advisory, Growth Advocacy, and Customer Enablement.

 - Have the CSM Team Lead independently owning daily CSM execution, coaching, and account quality.

 - Demonstrate measurable results from customer interventions and show that repeated one-to-one work is becoming reusable Advisory output, education, enablement, or product insight.

 - Have shipped multiple scaled programs and made concrete hiring or investment decisions for the function.


WITHIN THE FIRST TWELVE MONTHS

 - RevenueCat has a trusted, actively used system for serving high-value, high-potential, specialist-assisted, and scaled customers.

 - Customer Growth produces measurable improvement in customer outcomes, meaningful product adoption, account health, renewal readiness, expansion quality, and customer revenue outcomes.

 - The Head remains directly connected to customers and is a trusted executive partner for selected strategic accounts.

 - The best customer work consistently becomes reusable product, education, and market leverage.

 - The function has a strong leadership bench and a record of shipping improvements without waiting for perfect information.


WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

 - Approximately 10 or more years in Customer Success, Customer Growth, strategic accounts, Growth Advisory, product growth, lifecycle, monetization, or an adjacent customer-facing function.

 - Evidence of owning an entire function or multi-lane operating model, not only managing an individual CSM team.

A founder has heard about Daily Payouts and wants to understand whether it could help. They all reach out to RevenueCat, and they all deserve a useful conversation. You’re that conversation.

As a Product Expert, your job is to understand what someone is trying to accomplish, explain and demo the relevant parts of RevenueCat, and help them take a sensible next step. Sometimes that means helping them get started themselves. Sometimes it means bringing in an Account Executive, a Sales Engineer, Support, or someone else.

This is a new role at the intersection of inbound sales, product education, and helping developers get started. You’ll own the inbound conversations that don’t go directly to our Account Executives or Sales Engineers, and help us build a great experience for the people behind them.

You might be early in your career, building apps on the side, or looking to turn your product knowledge into a more customer-facing job. You don’t need to have held this exact role before. You do need to know RevenueCat well, enjoy talking to people, and have good judgment about what would actually help them.

We’re initially hiring one person in EMEA and one in the Americas. You’ll initially report to our Sales Engineering lead and learn alongside teammates who have been handling these conversations for years. You’ll also help shape how the Product Expert team works as it grows.

What you’ll be responsible for:

 - Make a great first impression. Respond to inbound interest, run useful discovery conversations, and understand the app, the people building it, their goals, and what they need from us.

 - Turn product knowledge into practical guidance. Give clear demos, answer questions, and connect the relevant parts of RevenueCat to someone’s situation. Help them understand the product, its limits, and what getting started involves.

 - Help straightforward adoption move forward. Guide people through the next steps they can take themselves, share useful resources, and follow up so a good conversation turns into progress.

 - Recognize the right next step. Bring qualified commercial opportunities to an Account Executive and involve a Sales Engineer for deeper technical discovery, complex migrations, or solution design. Connect support questions and people who aren’t ready yet with the appropriate team or follow-up. Understand (and tell people) when RevenueCat is not right for them.

 - Make handoffs easy for the customer. Keep clear notes on goals, requirements, open questions, and next steps. Stay responsible for follow-through until the next owner has picked up the conversation, so the customer doesn’t have to start over.

 - Help us improve the experience. Share recurring questions and feedback with the team. Turn what you learn into better demos, resources, and playbooks, and help us see where conversations or handoffs get stuck.

What you’ll need to be successful:

 - Strong, hands-on knowledge of RevenueCat. You can show how you’ve used the product and explain it in your own words. We care about what you understand and can demonstrate, whether you learned it at work or through your own projects.

 - Curiosity about the app business. You want to understand how developers build products, make money, and grow, and how RevenueCat can help.

 - Clear, friendly communication. You listen carefully, ask useful questions, write concise follow-ups, and explain the same idea differently to a developer, founder, or growth lead.

 - Technical common sense. You’re comfortable discussing SDKs, APIs, subscriptions, and paywalls at a practical level. You can recognize when a question needs an engineer and bring them in with useful context.

 - Commercial common sense. You can spot a promising opportunity, understand why timing and fit matter, and recommend a useful next step without making every conversation a pitch.

 - Ownership and follow-through. You can manage several conversations, keep your notes and commitments straight, and make sure people hear back from you.

 - The ability to work remotely and keep learning. You communicate proactively, ask for help when you need it, and can work hours that meaningfully overlap with customers and teammates in your region.

We’re more interested in your product knowledge, judgment, and helpfulness than a particular degree, job title, or number of years on your résumé.

Ideally, you:

 - Have built or shipped an app using RevenueCat, including a side project or Shipaton entry.

 - Have helped people through support, community participation, teaching, demos, or another customer-facing role.

 - Have experience with developer tools, subscriptions, or a product with both self-service and sales-assisted customers.

 - Enjoy improving a process or creating a resource that makes the next person’s job easier.

What success looks like:

Within the first month, you’ll:

 - Deepen your RevenueCat knowledge, shadow customer conversations, and learn how Sales, Support, and other parts of the business work together.

 - Start handling conversations with support from the team and learn when to bring in a specialist.

 - Host one of our bi-weekly demo stream, for a live audience of customers and prospects.

Within the first three months, you’ll:

 - Independently run the inbound discovery conversations and demos in your coverage area.

 - Help people get started and make well-qualified handoffs with clear context and next steps.

 - Build a reliable follow-up rhythm and agree with the team how we’ll measure response quality, opportunity progression, and adoption.

Within the first six months, you’ll:

 - Be a trusted source of product guidance for prospects and teammates.

 - Show how your work helps people move from interest to a useful next step, and use feedback and data to improve the experience.

 - Contribute reusable guidance that helps the team handle common questions and situations more effectively.

Within the first twelve months, you’ll:

 - Have helped establish how the Product Expert team runs discovery, demos, follow-up, and handoffs.

 - Help new teammates get up to speed and bring customer insight into how we improve the product and our processes.

 - Be building deeper expertise around your interests and strengths, with a foundation that could lead toward Sales Engineering, Account Executive, or Customer Success work over time.


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

 - 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

 - A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

 - Paid desk at a co-working space

title: Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition
description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. 

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. 

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.


THE ROLE

As Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition, you'll explore an important extension of how RevenueCat helps developers grow: helping them not just monetize the users they have, but acquire more of the right users in the first place.

RevenueCat already has several footholds in user acquisition, including our Apple Ads integration and integrations across the attribution and MMP ecosystem. But we're still early in defining what a broader RevenueCat user acquisition product should become. You'll be the first dedicated product hire focused on this space, reporting directly to our product lead for Ads, with significant latitude to shape both the strategy and the products we build.

This is a zero-to-one role: you won’t inherit a predetermined roadmap. You’ll own the discovery and delivery of products that help app developers acquire users. We’re looking for someone who has identified customer problems, made difficult prioritization decisions, and partnered with engineering and design to ship products customers use. Your experience in acquisition and measurement will inform which problems we pursue and how we solve them.

RevenueCat has some unusual advantages to build from: relationships with a large ecosystem of app developers, deep visibility into subscription and monetization outcomes, infrastructure already embedded in apps, and a growing advertising business. The challenge is figuring out how those assets can translate into something uniquely valuable for developers trying to grow.


ABOUT YOU:

 - You have 5+ years of experience owning product decisions end-to-end, including discovering customer problems, deciding what to build, partnering with engineering and design, shipping, and evaluating outcomes. Your title may have been Product Manager, founder, or something else; you can demonstrate personal responsibility for products used by external customers.

 - You bring relevant experience in mobile user acquisition, attribution, measurement, or advertising products. You understand how mobile acquisition teams work, the tools they rely on, and the trade-offs they face. You may have developed this expertise by building products for acquisition teams or by working directly in acquisition.

 - Experience building products for acquisition teams—such as attribution, measurement, advertising platforms, or acquisition analytics—is especially valuable. Hands-on campaign management is a plus.

 - You understand the modern mobile acquisition stack, including MMPs and attribution, Apple Ads, Meta and Google advertising products, conversion APIs, and related measurement infrastructure.

 - You can reason clearly about attribution, performance-marketing economics, and privacy. You understand concepts such as CAC, LTV, ROAS, optimization signals, ATT, SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit, consent management, and how downstream behavior should influence acquisition decisions.

 - You thrive in zero-to-one environments. You can take a large, ambiguous opportunity, identify the most important unanswered questions, narrow it into product bets, and find pragmatic ways to test those bets before making large investments.

 - You are sufficiently technical to work closely with engineering on integrations, APIs, SDKs, data flows, identity, attribution, and other technical product decisions.

 - You communicate clearly across different audiences and media, particularly in writing.


IN THE FIRST MONTH, YOU'LL:

 - Spend significant time with developers understanding how they acquire users today, how they evaluate acquisition performance, and where the process is painful, expensive, fragmented, or opaque.

 - Build a deep understanding of RevenueCat's existing acquisition-related products, integrations, data, customer research, and technical capabilities.

 - Build strong working relationships with engineering, design, data, go-to-market, and other product teams whose work intersects with user acquisition.

 - Develop a clear picture of the acquisition ecosystem, the problems RevenueCat is particularly well positioned to solve, and the biggest assumptions we still need to test.

 - Begin forming your own point of view on where RevenueCat could create differentiated value in user acquisition.


WITHIN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Have narrowed the broad user acquisition opportunity into a small number of concrete product hypotheses, grounded in customer research, market understanding, and RevenueCat's unique advantages.

 - Have a clear recommendation for where we should focus first — and why.

 - Begin validating that direction through prototypes, design partners, technical exploration, lightweight product experiments, or an initial shippable bet.

 - Establish a learning agenda that makes the biggest risks and unanswered questions explicit, and gives us a fast path to increasing or decreasing our conviction.

 - Align senior stakeholders around what we're testing, what we're not pursuing yet, and what evidence would cause us to change direction.


WITHIN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Have shipped our first substantive user acquisition product bet, or generated enough evidence to decisively change or stop it before making a larger investment.

 - Have real evidence from the market about where RevenueCat can — and cannot — create differentiated value.

 - Be independently driving product discovery, prioritization, and execution for the user acquisition area.

 - Have developed an evidence-backed point of view on the most promising opportunities in the space and what capabilities RevenueCat would need to pursue them.

 - Have turned a broad strategic opportunity into an increasingly focused product direction.


WITHIN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS, YOU'LL:

 - Have established a clear strategic direction for RevenueCat in user acquisition, supported by customer behavior and product evidence rather than thesis alone.

 - Have shipped meaningful products or experiments that either created measurable value for developers or materially changed our understanding of the opportunity—including changing or killing bets when the evidence didn’t support them.

 - Have a credible longer-term roadmap for turning the strongest early signals into a meaningful RevenueCat product area.

 - Be the primary IC product owner for User Acquisition and the internal domain expert on how app developers acquire, measure, and optimize users.

 - Have helped define how RevenueCat's monetization data, developer footprint, and advertising capabilities can work together to create a differentiated position in app growth.


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

 - 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

 - A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

 - 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

title: Software Engineer (Enterprise Experience, Backend)
description:
As a Backend Engineer on Coder's Enterprise Experience team, you'll build the features that help large organizations run Coder in production with confidence. The team owns what administrators and operators need to run Coder well. That covers how it scales, how it's upgraded, how reliably it performs, how it's observed and reported on, how activity is held accountable, and how it's secured.



You'll join a cross-functional team of backend, platform, and QA engineers who own the operator experience end to end. You'll ship features from design through production and partner with product and design to solve real operator problems.




WHAT YOU'LL DO HERE

 - Build features end to end, from a design you write within the team's existing approach through production rollout.

 - Write database migrations that follow the team's patterns for schema compatibility and safe upgrades.

 - Build the observability, reporting, and audit features administrators rely on to see what their deployment is doing.

 - Build features that keep enterprise deployments secure, following the team's security practices.

 - Help investigate and resolve scalability bottlenecks under production-like load, from database access patterns to concurrency in coderd.

 - Help resolve backend issues surfaced by Coder operators and administrators.

 - Document the features you build so a reviewer and the next engineer do not have to decode them.

 - Participate in code reviews, contribute to RFC-style design discussions, and join the on-call rotation.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2+ years of professional software engineering experience.

 - Professional experience writing and shipping Go.

 - Working understanding of Go's concurrency model, including goroutines, channels, and the sync package.

 - Comfortable with SQL, schema changes, and writing migrations.

 - Strong verbal and written communication skills, including surfacing blockers and uncertainty early.

 - Solid debugging skills and the persistence to work a problem, and to escalate early when stuck.

 - A self-motivated, analytical engineer who enjoys difficult technical challenges.




BONUS TACOS IF YOU HAVE

 - (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Experience investigating performance under real-world load, including debugging race conditions.

 - Experience with observability, audit, or security features in an enterprise product.

 - Experience with major cloud providers, Kubernetes, and container orchestration.

 - Experience building or operating distributed systems at a meaningful scale.

 - Curiosity about the latest developer tooling.




OUR TECH STACK

 - Backend: Go, Postgres, Kubernetes, gRPC

 - Observability: Prometheus, Grafana

 - CI/CD: GitHub Actions

 - General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.




INTERVIEW PROCESS 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.  

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.




OUR USE OF AI IN HIRING

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

 - Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

 - Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models.

In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf.

If you're applying for a role at Coder and have questions about how we use AI in our process, or if you'd like to request information about the data we collect, please contact careers@coder.com.

 


CODER IS A PROUD EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Senior Product Engineer (GCP)
description:
LOCALSTACK - THE LOCAL CLOUD SANDBOX FOR DEVELOPERS AND AI AGENTS

We are a fast-growing Series A startup building cutting-edge technology to revolutionize cloud development processes and support highly efficient dev&test feedback loops. We’ve closed our last $25mil round in Q4 2024, led by Notable Capital https://www.notablecap.com/, CRV https://www.crv.com/ and Heavybit https://www.heavybit.com/.

LocalStack is a local cloud development platform. LocalStack makes it easier, faster, and less expensive for software teams to ship reliable, high-quality applications to the cloud.

The cloud was built to run software, not to support AI-native development workflows. As the world's leading local cloud development platform, LocalStack provides secure local sandboxes that simulate cloud environments, enabling AI agents and software developers to find and fix risks faster and more effectively than they can in the cloud.

Our customer base ranges from SMBs to Global Fortune 500 companies. Our clients include companies like NASA, Harness, IBM, Workday, Comcast, Apple, 3M, Block and many more.

We are sustainably growing our globally distributed teams across GTM, operations and engineering. In 2025 we almost doubled in size and continue to grow across all areas in 2026.

👉Check our Notion Candidate Handbook https://localstack.notion.site/candidate-handbook-x-localstack and our GitHub https://github.com/localstack/localstack!

 - Scale MVP of the GCP emulator product into a GA ready product, owning full roadmap of the GCP emulator

 - Independently operate the agentic production line for GCP product

 - Instrument, measure and iterate on adoption, connecting directly with users and driving evidence based changes

 - Work closely with GTM team to integrate GCP emulator into a wider product suite offering: AWS / Snowflake, Azure, digital twins etc

✅ Experience we expect you to bring to the role

 - 7+ years professional software engineering or sales/solutions engineering in GCP context

 - In depth knowledge of GCP and exceptional understanding of how GCP is being used

 - High systems level fluency in what emulating a cloud actually requires: APIs, auth, resource models, distributed systems. Demonstrated strong system design thinking and experience.

 - Proficient in any language (Python, Go, Rust or some comparable language)

 - Experience with Claude/Gemini/Codex class tooling to ship solutions

 - Deep knowledge in containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and distribution mechanics: single binary packaging, cross platform builds, licensing / entitlement gating, telemetry instrumentation.

 - Experience in a product based environment with a strong product mindset, preferably VC backed Series B+ (devtooling or cloud infrastructure preferred)

🌱 Values we hold in LocalStack

 - Care: we create with compassion. We prioritize empathy and understanding in every interaction. By genuinely caring for our team, customers, and community, we create an environment where people thrive and impactful work flourishes

 - Ownership: we own the outcome. We take responsibility for our work and are passionate about its impact. We foster autonomy, inspire ambition, encourage ownership, and empower everyone to unlock their potential and make an impact.

 - Openness: we build trust together. We build trust through open communication and honest feedback. By sharing ideas and embracing diverse perspectives, we create stronger, more connected teams that work toward shared goals.

 - Courage: we dare to innovate. We embrace bold challenges and take calculated risks to move the needle. We step outside our comfort zones, experiment fearlessly, and turn setbacks into springboards for growth.

 - Excellence: we chase the extraordinary. We chase excellence by pushing boundaries and delivering results that go beyond the ordinary, constantly raising the bar and striving for greatness in everything we do. Excellence is not just the outcome, itʼs how we approach every task with purpose, passion, and a commitment to delivering exceptional value.

🎁 Benefits

 - Fully remote

 - Competitive salary

 - Annual company retreat

 - 2 extra company-wide holidays

 - Friendly and inclusive workplace culture (community guilds and online company events)


SOUNDS LIKE A GOOD MATCH?

We'd love to hear from you! Join us in shaping the future of cloud development at LocalStack.

To apply, follow the application process. Make sure to include a short motivation outlining why you are the perfect candidate for this role.

If your profile looks like a good match, our talent team will be in touch to organize further steps within 2 weeks.

Please note, that due to a high volume of candidates, we cannot offer personalized feedback to each candidate.

title: Software Engineer, Agents
description:
ABOUT LIVEKIT

LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the agentic era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe AI agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice and agentic AI applications for OpenAI, Salesforce, Spotify, Meta, and tens of thousands of other developers, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We are looking for an exceptional engineer to join the Agents team and help shape the future of agentic computing. You'll work on the core abstractions and infrastructure that developers use to build sophisticated AI agents; from real-time voice and text interactions to durable workflows and agent-to-agent communication.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and develop core functionality for the LiveKit Agents framework

 - Help define the text modality of the framework, enabling agents to interact with users across channels such as SMS

 - Design abstractions for stateful and durable agentic workflows, allowing agents to maintain state and coordinate work across interactions that may span minutes, hours, or longer

 - Shape agent-to-agent communication and delegation patterns, enabling voice agents to hand off tasks, collaborate, and compose into more sophisticated systems

 - Build simple, powerful developer APIs over complex distributed and real-time systems

 - Iterate quickly based on feedback from our developer community

 - Write clear documentation, examples, and reference implementations

 - Work primarily with Python and TypeScript




WHO YOU ARE

 - Experienced building LLM-based applications and agentic systems

 - Skilled at navigating complex systems and turning complexity into clean abstractions

 - Comfortable reasoning about state, concurrency and asynchronous workflows

 - Product-minded and excited about designing APIs and developer experiences

 - Experience building developer tools, frameworks, or SDKs is a plus

 - Interested in exploring emerging patterns in agent architecture rather than simply applying established ones

 - Comfortable working collaboratively in a remote environment





OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU

 - An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world

 - Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - Health, dental, and vision benefits

 - Flexible vacation policy



LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Distributed Systems

Founded in 2021, LiveKit has rapidly grown to support over 3 Billion calls annually, 100,000+ developers globally, and industry giants like OpenAI, Character AI, Spotify, and Meta.

 - Build libraries, protocols, and tooling that raise reliability and developer velocity across the org

 - Diagnose and harden critical paths using metrics, tracing, testing, and real-world traffic insights

 - Shape new platform capabilities across identity, scheduling, observability, and distributed state management

 - You think in terms of data flow, state, performance, and correctness, and you can reduce complex systems into understandable components

 - You value clear communication, practical engineering, and building systems that others enjoy working with




NICE TO HAVE
